title: A Moving Story, But It Won't Take You Away

contact_edits.before: Fathers and husbands are kept strictly off stage; the one male actor, Anthony Bekenn, is billed as the symbolic Rat-Catcher but actually appears as a series of officials -- German and English, terrifying or benevolent or in-between -- whom he renders as a series of neat music-hall sketches. These include a wartime postman, mentally lumping Jews with Germans as undesirable aliens and refusing to hear the difference. (This does make a point.) Cameron Porteous, perhaps in reference to the triple time-scheme, has designed a three-arched set that works well for the several scenes that are set in railway stations (with announcements recorded, I suspect, by the director himself ), less well for the more numerous scenes that are supposed to go on in confined spaces like the all-important attic. There are also projections, which are helpful in letting us know where we are but are not especially atmospheric; at the preview I attended, they vanished temporarily due to a computer breakdown, and I don't think that the play suffered much from their absence. I suspect that this play would work best in an intimate theatre with a minimum of design. - Kindertransport is at the Harold Green Theatre until Nov. 23. For tickets and information call 416-366-7723 or visit hgjewishtheatre.com.
